I've finished the calculation from the official BTS monthly file, so here are the results.

## SFO departures, July 2025 (mainline carriers)

| Airline | Departures counted | Avg departure delay (min) | Share delayed more than 15 min |
|---|---|---|---|
| United (UA) | 5,059 | 12.7 | 20.5% (1,037) |
| Alaska (AS) | 1,020 | 10.6 | 21.5% (219) |
| Delta (DL) | 1,224 | 14.0 | 23.6% (289) |
| Southwest (WN) | 700 | 21.9 | 37.9% (265) |

**Average delay definition.** The averages above use BTS's signed `DepDelay`, so early departures count as negative minutes. If you average `DepDelayMinutes` instead (early departures set to 0, which many sites use), you get UA 15.7, AS 13.7, DL 17.2 and WN 22.8. Pick one and label it on the slide.

## Source
- **Dataset:** BTS (Bureau of Transportation Statistics, US DOT) "Airline On-Time Performance Data", the Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987–present) table. It is the raw flight-level file behind the DOT Air Travel Consumer Report.
- **File:** `https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_2025_7.zip`. I downloaded it directly and the CSV inside is dated 14 Oct 2025.
- **My filter:** `Origin = SFO`, grouped by `Reporting_Airline`. I kept flights with a recorded departure delay, so cancelled flights are excluded.
- **Share delayed:** flights with `DepDelayMinutes` greater than 15, divided by flights with a recorded departure delay. The BTS "15 minutes or more" convention gives slightly higher shares: UA 21.3%, AS 22.1%, DL 24.3%, WN 39.7%.
- **Calculation:** I computed these myself from the raw file, using a script I wrote. BTS doesn't publish this airport-by-airline breakdown as a ready-made table, so please don't cite it as a figure BTS published.

## Caveats
- **Regional flights are not included.** BTS reports by operating carrier. United, Alaska and Delta flights flown by regional partners show up under that partner. At SFO, SkyWest (`OO`) had 2,951 departures, 20.6% of them delayed more than 15 minutes, with an average delay of 10.6 minutes. If your slide says "United" in the passenger sense, the numbers will differ.
- **The file may have been revised.** BTS can revise monthly files after release. This is the version available now.

I couldn't get any of this from the California Secretary of State, so I have no entity numbers, statuses, filing dates or agents to give you.

- **What I tried:** the SOS business search (bizfile Online, `bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov`) is the official source. A direct request to its search API returned an Incapsula bot-protection challenge instead of data. A Firecrawl browser scrape of the search page failed with "website is blocking automated access."
- **Why I stopped:** getting past that block would mean working around the site's access controls. I didn't think that was my call to make for a vendor check.
- **Why I left the fields empty:** I could recall some of these from memory or from third-party aggregators like OpenCorporates. You asked for official SOS data only, and memory is the wrong basis for a pre-signing check. Some of these companies are also Delaware corporations registered in CA as foreign entities, so their CA numbers, status and agent details are exactly what could be wrong. I'd rather leave them blank than hand you unverified values.

**Ways to get the data:**
1. **Search it yourself (about 5 minutes).** Go to bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/search/business and search each name. Then open the result and its detail drawer. It shows the entity number, status, formation state ("Jurisdiction"), initial filing date and agent for service of process. If you send me the five results, I can put them in a comparison table and flag anything odd, such as a suspended or forfeited status or a name mismatch like "Vercel Inc." versus the registered name.
2. **Get a formal record.** If you need something for the contract file, you can order a Certificate of Status from the SOS. Those are the strongest evidence of good standing.
3. **Use an authorized channel.** If you have an approved way to reach the site programmatically, such as an allowlisted IP or the SOS's bulk data or API program, tell me and I'll run the queries that way.

Also check the exact legal names on each vendor's contract draft. For example, "Rippling People Center Inc." may be registered under a slightly different name than the one in your list.

| **23V858000** | Fuel system: fuel pump | The in-tank fuel pump may fail and stall the engine while driving. This is a second, broader fuel pump recall. |
| **24V064000** | Air bags: front passenger occupant sensor | The passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit. The air bag may then not be suppressed as intended and could deploy unintentionally in a crash. |
| **26V332000** | Air bags: front passenger occupant sensor | This is the same weight-sensor defect, filed in May 2026. It covers more Honda and Acura models and years. |

- **Which recalls apply:** Recalls apply to specific VINs, not whole model years. Some of these may not cover a particular car, and the 2020 coupe, sedan and hatchback are covered differently. Before you buy, run the car's VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.
- **Open recalls:** The VIN lookup also shows whether each recall has already been fixed. Honda dealers do the repairs for free, so ask the seller for proof the work was done. If any are still open, you could make fixing them a condition of the sale.
- **Fuel pump recalls:** 21V215000 and 23V858000 are separate campaigns. A car fixed under the first could still be covered by the second, so check both.

Stripe shipped breaking changes in only two API versions in 2025. Under their versioning model, each named release (Basil, Clover) puts all its breaking changes in its first version. Stripe says the monthly versions after that are additive only.

I read the Basil and Clover changelog pages, then opened every entry dated 2025-03-31 or 2025-09-30 (about 85 pages) and kept the ones whose page title carries the "Breaking changes" tag. I did not open the monthly entries from April to August and from October to December 2025, so their additive-only status rests on Stripe's statement. The Clover entry for 2026-01-28 reverses one Basil change; I note it below.

## 2025-03-31.basil (March 31, 2025)

Stripe's summary calls this "a significant number of breaking changes."

**Billing**
- **Coupons:** You can no longer create `amount_off` coupons with `duration: forever`, or apply existing ones to subscriptions, invoices, quotes, Checkout Sessions and similar objects. The 2026-01-28.clover version brings this back.
- **Singular discount parameters:** The `coupon` and `promotion_code` parameters are removed in favor of `discounts`, which supports stacking.
- **Subscription periods:** `current_period_start` and `current_period_end` are removed from the Subscription. Each subscription item now carries its own billing period.
- **Upcoming Invoice API:** `GET /v1/invoices/upcoming` is removed. Use Create Preview Invoice instead. You also can't preview one invoice across all of a customer's subscriptions anymore.
- **Legacy usage-based billing:** Removed. You can't create `metered` prices without a `meter`. `billing_thresholds` and `aggregate_usage` are gone from all endpoints.
- **Invoice pricing:** Top-level price fields on Invoice Items and Invoice Line Items are replaced by a polymorphic `pricing` object.
- **Invoice taxes:** Top-level tax fields are replaced by `taxes` on line items and `total_taxes` on Invoices and Credit Notes.
- **Partial payments:** Invoices and credit notes now support multiple (partial) payments and track over-payments.
- **`parent` field:** New on invoices, invoice items and line items. It shows which upstream object generated them.

**Checkout and payments**
- **`shipping_details`:** On a Checkout Session, it moved to `collected_information.shipping_details`.
- **Subscription-mode Checkout Sessions:** The subscription is now created after payment completes. This lowers latency and changes how a session can be updated.
- **Partial capture or cancellation:** These no longer create a `Refund` object.
- **Interac:** `interac_present` no longer supports `manual` capture.
- **Naver Pay:** You can set its PaymentMethod fields only when you create the object. Later updates are no longer allowed.
- **Payment Element:** The default layout changed from `tabs` to `accordion`. A `defaultCollapsed` value left undefined now collapses when several payment methods are shown.
- **Vault and Forward API:** It returns `402` instead of `502` or `504` for upstream timeouts.

**Platform-wide and other**
- **`total_count` expansion:** You can't expand it on lists anymore. Doing so returns a 400 `property_forbidden` error, and the restriction also applies to new users on earlier versions.
- **Connect `Person.political_exposure`:** It changed from a string to an enum.
- **Connect error codes:** New values, such as `information_missing` and `invalid_signator`, appear in `requirements.errors`.
- **Issuing webhooks:** Real-time authorization webhooks now send `Accept: application/json`.
- **Issuing authorizations:** Authorizations that Stripe expires now get status `expired` instead of `reversed`. A new `network_fallback` value is added to `request_history.reason`.

## 2025-09-30.clover (September 30, 2025)

**Billing**
- **Billing mode:** Flexible billing mode is now the default for new subscriptions. Set `billing_mode.type=classic` to keep the old behavior.
- **Subscription schedules:** The `phases.iterations` parameter is removed. Use `duration`. A phase's computed `end_date` now also accounts for billing-cycle-anchor changes.
- **Promotion Codes:** The top-level `coupon` field moved to `promotion.coupon`.
- **Discount object:** The auto-expanded `coupon` property is removed and a `source` hash is added (`type`, `coupon`).

**Checkout and Elements**
- **`currency_conversion`:** Removed from Checkout Sessions. Use `presentment_details`.
- **`redirectToCheckout`:** Removed from Stripe.js.
- **`initCheckout`:** It is now synchronous.
- **Postal codes:** They are no longer collected for card payments in Canada, the UK and Puerto Rico, on Checkout and Payment Element.
- **Deprecated Stripe.js elements:** The Affirm and Afterpay messaging elements and the bank-collection element are removed. Use the Payment Method Messaging Element and the Payment Element.
- **Saved payment methods:** Elements with Checkout Sessions now enable and redisplay them by default when a customer ID is passed.
- **Client secrets:** Elements won't initialize with a PaymentIntent or SetupIntent client secret in `succeeded`, `canceled`, `processing`, `requires_capture` or `requires_action` state with non-detachable payment methods (Boleto and similar).

**Payments, Radar, Issuing, Connect**
- **Stablecoin payments:** PaymentIntents confirmed with `crypto` now go to `processing` once submitted.
- **Decline codes:** They changed for Alma, Amazon Pay, Billie, Satispay and the South Korean payment methods.
- **Radar:** `closed_reason` gained `acknowledged` and `payment_never_settled`.
- **Issuing risk levels:** They were renamed to standard values (`unknown`, `not_assessed`, `low` and so on).
- **Connect:** `requirements.errors` gets an `unsupported_business_type` code and an `external_hold` code. There are also new `notice` resolution paths for legal, PEP and sanctions reviews. These were previously reported as `other_supportability_inquiry` or `other_compliance_inquiry`.

Because you pin your version, the changes most likely to affect your code are the Basil subscription period fields, the Upcoming Invoice removal, the legacy metered-billing removal, the coupon and `discounts` changes, and Clover's flexible billing default.

I computed these from the raw BTS On-Time Performance file for July 2025, filtered to departures from SFO.

| Carrier | Departures (non-cancelled) | Avg departure delay (min) | Share delayed 15+ min | Share delayed more than 15 min |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| United (UA) | 5,059 | **15.7** | **21.3%** | 20.5% |
| Alaska (AS) | 1,020 | **13.7** | **22.1%** | 21.5% |
| Delta (DL) | 1,224 | **17.2** | **24.3%** | 23.6% |
| Southwest (WN) | 700 | **22.8** | **39.7%** | 37.9% |

**Source**
- The dataset is the Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) "Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance (1987–present)" table. It sits in the DOT Transtats database, and this is the data behind the DOT Air Travel Consumer Report.
- I downloaded the July 2025 file from `https://transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_2025_7.zip`.
- I kept rows where `Origin = SFO` and `Reporting_Airline` was UA, AS, DL or WN.
- I excluded cancelled flights, which have no departure delay. Diverted flights that did depart are included.
- Each average is the mean of `DepDelayMinutes`. BTS counts early departures as 0 in that field.
- If you average the signed `DepDelay` instead, early departures offset late ones. The means then come out lower: UA 12.7, AS 10.6, DL 14.0 and WN 21.9 minutes.
- BTS's own delayed-flight flag (`DepDel15`) means a delay of 15 minutes or more. That gives the bold column. You asked for more than 15 minutes, so I also counted `DepDelayMinutes > 15`, which gives the last column. For a slide, "15+ minutes" matches the BTS definition.

**Caveats**
- Regional partners that report separately are not included, because they file under their own carrier codes. That means SkyWest flying as United Express and Alaska's partner Horizon. United's figure is mainline only, and Alaska's is probably missing a large share of its SFO flying. SkyWest (OO) alone had 2,951 departures at SFO in July, which would change the picture.
- Southwest has the smallest sample, at about 700 departures.
- I haven't cross-checked these against a published BTS summary table. They come straight from the raw file.

NHTSA lists 5 recalls for the 2020 Honda Civic. I pulled them from NHTSA's recalls-by-vehicle API (make=honda, model=civic, year=2020). Most of these recalls cover many Honda and Acura models, not just the Civic. Each one applies to certain vehicles within the range, so check your specific VIN.

| Campaign # | Component | Problem | Date reported |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21V215000 | Fuel system: fuel pump | The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank may fail, which can stall the engine while driving. | 2021-03-25 |
| 23V458000 | Service brakes: master cylinder | A tie rod fastener between the brake booster and master cylinder may have been assembled improperly. The master cylinder can separate and cause loss of braking. | 2023-06-29 |
| 23V858000 | Fuel system: fuel pump | The in-tank fuel pump may fail, which can stall the engine while driving. This is a broader, later fuel pump recall than 21V215000. | 2023-12-18 |
| 24V064000 | Air bags: front passenger occupant sensor | The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack and short circuit. It can then fail to suppress the air bag as intended. | 2024-02-01 |
| 26V332000 | Air bags: front passenger occupant sensor | The same weight sensor may crack and short circuit, which can make the air bags deploy unintentionally during a crash. | 2026-05-21 |

Before you buy:
- **VIN check:** Run the car's VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, or ask a Honda dealer. This tells you which of these recalls apply to that car and whether the repair was done. Recall repairs are free at dealers.
- **Most recent recall:** 26V332000 is from May 2026. The seller may not have had it done, so confirm it specifically.
- **Fuel pump recalls:** There are two (21V215000 and 23V858000). A car can be covered by one and not the other, so check both.

Stripe shipped breaking changes in only two API versions in 2025. Every other 2025 release is additive and says so on the changelog page. I couldn't open the individual entries (the page returned a captcha, and I didn't try to get around it). The descriptions below come from the entry titles on the Basil and Clover changelog pages, so read each linked entry before you bump your pin.

The changelog lists everything in these two releases under a "Breaking changes" heading, including purely additive items. I've split them into likely breaking and additive.

## 1. `2025-03-31.basil` (March 31, 2025)

Stripe describes it as "a significant number of breaking changes". Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/basil

**Likely breaking (removals, replacements, behavior changes):**
- **Coupons:**
  - Discount coupons without an end time are no longer supported (`restrict-coupon-duration`).
  - The singular `coupon` and `promotion_code` parameters are removed in favor of stackable discounts (`deprecate-singular-coupon-promotion-code`).
- **Invoices:**
  - Top-level price fields are replaced by new price modeling on Invoice Items and Invoice Line Items.
  - Top-level tax properties are replaced by new tax modeling on Invoices, Invoice Line Items and Credit Note Line Items.
  - Invoices now support multiple partial payments.
- **Subscriptions:** Billing periods move to the subscription item level, and the subscription-level `current_period_start` and `current_period_end` are removed.
- **Invoicing resources:** They gain a `parent` field showing how they were generated.
- **Billing removals:**
  - The Upcoming Invoice API methods are replaced by the Create Preview Invoice API.
  - Legacy usage-based billing is removed.
- **Lists:** You can no longer expand `total_count` on list methods (`deprecate-total-count-expansion`).
- **Page parameter:** The `page` parameter is removed (`remove-page-event-destinations`).
- **Checkout:**
  - Checkout Sessions drop their shipping details field.
  - Subscription Checkout Sessions now create the subscription only after payment, with new update semantics and lower latency (`checkout-legacy-subscription-upgrade`).
- **Payments:**
  - The manual capture method is removed for Interac cards.
  - Partially capturing or canceling a payment no longer creates a Refund.
  - Naver Pay payment method fields can't be modified after creation.
  - The Vault and Forward API returns 402 for upstream timeouts.
- **Webhooks:** Issuing authorization webhooks now send a JSON `Accept` header.
- **Connect and Elements:**
  - The Person object's political exposure property changes from a string to an enum.
  - The Payment Element's default layout changes.

**Additive, listed in the same release:**
- New webhook events for billing meters and credits, and a `last` aggregation formula for meters.
- A `custom` `ui_mode` and `initCheckout` for Checkout Sessions.
- New payment methods: Billie, Satispay, NZ BECS and Naver Pay saving.
- New error codes, new customer balance transaction types, new Issuing reason codes and an `expired` status.
- Checkout permissions, optional items and shipping option updates.
- Terminal WiFi configuration.

## 2. `2025-09-30.clover` (September 30, 2025)

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/clover

**Likely breaking:**
- **Checkout:**
  - The currency conversion field is removed from Checkout Sessions.
  - `redirectToCheckout` is removed.
  - `initCheckout` becomes synchronous.
  - The postal code is removed for card payments in certain regions.
- **Elements:**
  - Saved payment method defaults change in Elements with Checkout Sessions.
  - Client secrets for Intents in certain states can't be reused when initializing Elements.
  - Deprecated messaging and bank elements are removed.
- **Billing:**
  - The `iterations` parameter is removed from subscription schedules.
  - Promotion Codes now reference Coupons through a polymorphic `promotion` field.
  - Discounts gain a `source` property and lose the `coupon` property.
  - Flexible billing mode becomes the default for new subscriptions.
  - Subscription schedule phase end dates now account for billing cycle anchor changes.
- **Payments:**
  - Decline codes change for Alma, Amazon Pay, Billie, Satispay and South Korean payment methods.
  - Submitted stablecoin payments gain a processing status.
- **Issuing:** Authorization risk levels are updated to standard values.
- **Connect:**
  - Risk requirement descriptions are more specific for legal, PEP and sanctions review.
  - There is a new error code for business type validation.

**Additive, listed in the same release:**
- Balance Settings API, name collection on Checkout and Customers, excluding payment methods, per-method capture method, and Checkout branding settings.
- MB WAY, the customer portal trial behavior, itemized proration discounts, new Radar enum values, and the Klarna chargeback loss reason.
- Japan Terminal Location fields, BBPOS WisePad 3 splash screens, an Issuing card second line, and the crypto `cash` value.
- The Elements developer assistant, the tax calculation provider setting, and new Financial Connections error codes.

## Not breaking

The monthly releases are additive only: `2025-04-30`, `05-28`, `06-30`, `07-30` and `08-27.basil`, and `2025-10-29`, `11-17` and `12-15.clover`. The January and February 2025 Acacia releases (`2025-01-27` and `2025-02-24`) are also additive.

To check each item before upgrading, open the linked entries. The URLs follow `https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/<basil|clover>/<date>/<slug>`, and the page source is saved in `.firecrawl/stripe-basil.md` and `.firecrawl/stripe-clover.md`.

- **Student counts to treat with care:**

  - Yeh lists 7 people with no degree labels.
  - Li's 5 aren't labeled by degree, though none is marked as a postdoc.
  - Wu's 5 and You's 3 are new students starting Fall 2026.
- **Papers:** Ruizhe Zhang's only 2025 item is an arXiv preprint, since published in 2026. Bullins and Yeh list the same paper, as co-authors.
